newsitem.title: FRANCE: Borotra calls for new talks with Renault.
newsitem.headline: Borotra calls for new talks with Renault.

text.p: French Industry Minister Franck Borotra told parliament on Tuesday that he was inviting car maker Renault for new talks over the financing of an industrial restructuring plan.

Last week, the French government told Renault and PSA Peugeot Citroen that it could not agree with a plan proposed by the car firms to finance part of a project which envisaged some 40,000 early retirements in exchange for hiring younger staff.

"Contrary to what has been suggested, the Industry Minister was not involved nor consulted about the decision of the management of Renault (to shut a plant in Belgium and axe French jobs)," he said during question time.

"The Industry Minister, at the request of the Prime Minister, is asking Renault's management to renew discussions with the authorities, and to enter into talks with employees, to put into place the necessary financial means for the industrial restructuring, as well as to find social solutions that limit the consequences of this restructuring," he said.
He said the talks and financial plan were needed because of the "economic, industrial and above all human" consequences of the decision to cut jobs.
